deck_title: Bragg-Fabry-Perot Delta = 2*n_f*d*cos(theta_t) thin-film cosine blue-shift law vs naive angle-invariant tint rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Thomas Young (1801), Charles Fabry & Alfred Pérot (1899), and W. L. Bragg (1913) thin-film interference cosine blue-shift law (round-trip optical path difference Delta_OPD = 2 * n_f * d * cos(theta_t) shifting constructive peak wavelength as lambda_peak = lambda_0 * cos(theta_t) = lambda_0 / (1 + u) across secant obliquity excess u = sec(theta_t) - 1 in [0.000, 1.000], locking lambda_active / lambda_Bragg = 1.0000x across all 17 stations with 0/17 violated) versus naive angle-invariant metallic tint shader (keeping lambda = lambda_0 regardless of cos(theta_t), which overestimates constructive peak wavelength by sec(theta_t) = 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x at S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-layer normal wavevector k_z phase accumulation quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: 3D Morpho butterfly wings, jewel-beetle elytra, dichroic camera lens coatings, pearl nacre, and soap-bubble iridescence shaders
Evaluating exact round-trip optical path difference Delta_OPD = 2 * n_f * d * cos(theta_t) so grazing angles shift constructive interference toward blue/violet
Avoiding the common graphics bug of multiplying by 1/cos(theta_t) (geometric ray length) instead of cos(theta_t) (normal wavevector projection)
not_for: Angle-independent bulk pigment absorption (Lambertian painted walls)
Pure geometric mirror reflections without dielectric thin-film layers
